solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Staggered out of Belfast bar drunk around midnight with journalist

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the next item
someone drunk lurches about, so the letters before it stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder
the middle letter of the word night, the 'mid' of night
ED is short for editor, the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles out of a Belfast pub, drunk, around midnight, accompanied by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the pub's name and the bar are shuffled; the midnight letter is slotted into the shuffled result before the journalist is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbergasted means astonished, and staggered is used in the same sense of being stunned by surprise.

clue.text: Pagan using axe without resistance initially slays more with it

parts.note: to axe and to fire both mean to dismiss
w/o is the written abbreviation of without
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: initially keeps only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of slays
hip means with it, so more with it is hipper

explanation.surface: A heathen wields an axe, and with no opposition kills more people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a container instruction but stands for its abbreviation w/o.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-worshipper venerates fire as a god, a non-Christian believer in the old sense of pagan.

clue.text: Against sudden speeding up of a new children's game

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
tig is the British name for the chasing game tag

explanation.surface: An objection to suddenly hurrying up a fresh playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tig, also called tag, is a game where one child chases and touches the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-g describes equipment such as a pilot's suit that counters the g-forces of rapid acceleration.

clue.text: Singing with US composer's hard work!

parts.note: Samuel Barber, American composer, with the possessive S
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
op. is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A remark that an American composer's piece is tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Barber wrote the Adagio for Strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied singing, typically by male quartets.

clue.text: Faraway state, one toured by US patriot

indicators.note: a place toured by someone has that visitor travelling within it, so the patriot holds it

parts.note: Paul Revere, hero of the American Revolution's midnight ride
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A distant land, one visited on a tour by an American hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Faraway state looks like a distant country, but it means a dreamy frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, when the mind drifts far off, so it is a faraway mental condition.

clue.text: Complaint from porter maybe intended to be picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard by the ear, so the sounds count, not the spelling

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an ale, and intended is meant

explanation.surface: A grievance from a railway porter, meant for collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a luggage carrier but is the beer; 'maybe' marks ale as a general term for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a medical word for an illness or disorder, which is what an ailment is.

clue.text: Bank on relations turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: re means on or about
it is slang for sex, sexual relations

explanation.surface: Counting on your family to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank on looks like a phrase meaning rely on, but bank is the definition and on is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a row of things, such as a bank of seats, which is one tier.

clue.text: Peddles old, mainly forged, legal documents

indicators.note: forged means hammered into shape, so the letters are beaten into a new order
mainly means most of it, so the last letter of old is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone sells counterfeit antique legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Forged looks like the forgery of documents in the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is a legal document made by one person, used in Britain to change one's name.

clue.text: One's O so unloved, a Romeo in awful despair, ultimately!

indicators.note: awful means in a terrible state, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of despair

parts.note: the last letter of despair

explanation.surface: Someone so unloved, a Romeo in deep despair, cries 'Oh!'
explanation.walkthrough: O looks like a cry of anguish but is the blood group.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with blood group O negative can give blood to patients of any group, so they are universal donors.

clue.text: Men on bunk, one turning round

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, which is rot
OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers lounging on their bunks while one of them spins about.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'Men on bunk' puts the men after the bunk. Bunk here is the noun for nonsense, not a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine such as a helicopter or engine, so it is literally something rotating.

clue.text: See mischievous kids cut adolescent's cloth

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for mischievous kids loses its final letter

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references
elves are mischievous little folk
a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: Telling someone to look at naughty children who have cut up a teenager's fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids here are little folk, not children or young goats. The 's after adolescent reads as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Velveteen is a cotton fabric with a short pile imitating velvet, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Brother in film industry visited by a brother who supports the family?

indicators.note: a place visited by someone has that visitor inside it, so the film word takes the rest in

parts.note: one of the Warner Brothers of the Hollywood studio
taken as written
'Brother!' as an exclamation of surprise is the same as 'Gee!'

explanation.surface: A Hollywood movie mogul's sibling drops in on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The second brother is an exclamation of surprise, not a relative, and the visitors sit just after the studio's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage earner is the person whose paid job keeps a household; the question mark admits the description is broad.

clue.text: Unscrupulous dealer of dope meeting two Roman couples?

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is inside information, slang dope
two couples make four, which is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shady drug dealer meets two Italian couples.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope means information here, not drugs; SP for starting price is a racing tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook trading in black-market goods, a shady trader.

clue.text: Critical of hint accompanying repair

parts.note: a touch is a slight trace, a hint
and means along with
to repair to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about a suggested fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Repair means to go somewhere, as in 'repair to the drawing room', not to mend.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-and-go describes an uncertain, risky situation, as a patient's condition is critical.

clue.text: Note manned satellite oddly used for launch again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the International Space Station, a crewed satellite

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions, the first, third and so on

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A space mission note: the crewed station was used in an odd way for a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to bring out again, as a publisher relaunches a book or record.

clue.text: Serving minister lying

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vicar or official currently holding the post
second meaning: reclining, resting on something

explanation.surface: A politician in office is telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying looks like dishonesty, but it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the holder of a church living or office, and as an adjective it can mean leaning or recumbent.

clue.text: One winding up thread's beginning with cylinder

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of thread

parts.note: first letter of thread
a roller is a cylinder

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a thread starting at a spool.
explanation.walkthrough: Winding up looks like coiling thread, but it means provoking: an online troll winds people up.
explanation.definitionFit: A troller posts provocative messages to annoy people, and to wind someone up is British slang for to tease or irritate.

clue.text: Threatens, perhaps, with ECT, or sending to shrink

indicators.note: shrinking the phrase trims it down to a run of letters lying within it

parts.note: the letters run across with, ECT, or and sending

explanation.surface: Bullying a patient with electric shocks or a referral to a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, matching ECT, but here it is the instruction. 'Perhaps' admits that threatening is one example of hectoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or browbeat, and threatening someone is one way of doing so.

clue.text: Water flowing from pipe down bottom of drain stopping soon

parts.note: sh! means be quiet, which is pipe down

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so the letter sits inside the word for soon

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry word is its last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of drain

explanation.surface: Water running out of a pipe down to the drain soon gets blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The N goes in after the first letter of ANON. 'Pipe down' looks like plumbing but is a call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland, so it is flowing water.

clue.text: Plant, such a fine one, ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener laments that such a lovely plant has been spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping pink and purple flowers, a garden plant.

clue.text: Hats passed round by artists

parts.note: to feed a ball is to pass it
O is round in shape
RAs, Royal Academicians, are artists

explanation.surface: Headgear handed round by a group of painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed round' looks like one phrase, but each word gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim.

clue.text: After passing examination at college, back for quiz?

indicators.note: back says the letters built so far are read from the end

parts.note: a post-mortem, the examination after one passes away
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: After getting through a college exam, a student returns for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like succeeding in an exam, but it means dying. Being up at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, an informal sense of quiz.

clue.text: Rated by female, with assistance secured

parts.note: to give a hand is to assist
to bag something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Given a rating by a woman, with help obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: Rate here is the old verb meaning to scold, not to score. Handbagging was the press word for Margaret Thatcher's verbal assaults on colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: To be handbagged is to be harshly berated, typically by a forceful woman, and rate is an old word for scold.

clue.text: To perform, raised leg on the table?

parts.note: to gig is to play a live show

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upward

explanation.surface: A performer's instruction to put a raised leg on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg here is meat served at a meal, not part of a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of lamb or mutton, cooked and served at a meal.

clue.text: Stone ring seen north of China

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of means placed above, so first in the order

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
china is rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a pal

explanation.surface: A gemstone ring spotted in northern China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is the country in the surface but Cockney rhyming slang for mate here.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, a precious stone set in rings.

clue.text: Revelation from you when probing English batsman

indicators.note: something probing pushes into the thing it examines, so it sits inside

parts.note: E for English plus an opener, a batsman who starts the innings
ye is the old word for you

explanation.surface: A surprising disclosure from you while questioning an England cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: YE goes in straight after the E. An opener is one of the two batsmen who start a cricket innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something startling that reveals the truth, a sudden revelation.

clue.text: Appreciate stylish invitation from dinner host?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Enjoy a smart invitation from the host of a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of the clue reads as one phrase; the definition is the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Dig in!' is what a host says to tell guests to start eating, an invitation to tuck in.

clue.text: Craftsman after camping equipment cornering small boy scout

indicators.note: after says the craftsman comes following everything else in the line
to corner someone is to hem them in, so the camping kit surrounds the boy

parts.note: a tent is camping gear
Al, a boy's short name
S is the abbreviation for small
a potter crafts clay

explanation.surface: A craftsman at a campsite traps a young lad who is a Boy Scout.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes outside the tent, after it. Scout looks like a Boy Scout, but it is the recruiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout searches for gifted performers or players, which is the job of a talent-spotter.
